content.title: About
content.content: Toasted challah is a traditional Jewish bread made from a yeasted dough, often served with egg. Toasting creates a crisp crust while the crumb stays soft and aromatic. It is commonly used for breakfasts, sandwiches, and as a base for egg dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Challah is braided, symbolizing unity and continuity.
Egg is traditionally added to the dough, giving it a golden hue and subtle richness.
Toasting enhances caramelization, producing a crunchy crust.
In Jewish culture challah is served on Shabbat and holidays.
Variants include raisins, poppy seeds, sesame, or plain.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: The bread provides sustained energy through slow-release glucose.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: B1, B2 and B3 support metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Egg in the dough adds complete animal protein, aiding tissue repair.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: Challah supplies iron, magnesium and phosphorus, important for bones and blood formation.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain versions support digestion and satiety.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional challah contains wheat, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Toasting and the added egg make the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some recipes include salt; individuals with hypertension should choose low‑salt versions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted challah can be served with butter, avocado, cheese, smoked salmon, or used as a base for sandwiches with egg, vegetables and spreads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep toasted challah in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage, freeze in a zip‑lock bag and reheat in the oven before serving.
